correctness.rationale: Let J=I-2P0 and R=I-2P. For every symmetric orthogonal projector P, the exact algebraic identity sym(RJ)=I-2(P-P0)^2 holds. The separability assumption gives J grad E=grad F, F=f+g, so dot F=-beta grad F^T RJ grad F <=-beta(1-2delta^2)||grad F||². Global mu-strong convexity implies the gradient-PL bound ||grad F||²>=2mu(F-F*); integrating gives the stated exact rate and a state-norm exponential estimate. Its compact sublevels prevent finite-time blowup for classical locally Lipschitz projectors. A rank-one planar projector rotated phi gives RJ a planar rotation by twice phi, so a quadratic achieves equality; at phi=pi/4 the flow is a pure rotation, at larger phi it expands. Embedding one mixed pair proves sharpness for all 1<=k<n. Exact rational projector identities, critical matrix and above-critical trace were checked independently, rather than treating the finite checker as proof of uniform dynamics.

Explicit periodic and expanding counterexamples prove genuine necessity, not just a sufficient inequality; separability is a natural but material restriction.

final_claim: For fixed split E=-f(u)+g(v) with f and g globally mu-strongly convex and exact negative subspace P0, any rank-k orthoprojector P(t,x) uniformly within delta<1/sqrt2 of P0 yields global exponential high-index saddle attraction with optimal F-energy exponent 2 beta mu(1-2delta^2); at delta=1/sqrt2 a quadratic yields periodic orbits and above it expanding spirals.
